early.on_plan: Cinderace active if in opener (Explosiveness); >=1 Duraludon + Relicanth benched; Turbo Flare used >=1; manual energy attach prioritizes the accelerator (Cinderace's 1 energy) over displayed-max Archaludon

mid.until: any Archaludon (bench or active) has metal >= 3
mid.on_plan: retreat Cinderace (retreat0, free) and PROMOTE Archaludon; first Metal Defender by turn 3 (accel) / turn 4 (planB); Full Metal Lab down; Hero's Cape on Archaludon

late.on_plan: Metal Defender every turn (>=1 KO per 2 turns), heal with Jumbo Ice Cream, keep wall; STOP non-essential digging when deckCount <= D; never promote Relicanth or unloaded Duraludon

doctrines.name: accel-milk
doctrines.plan: keep Cinderace active firing Turbo Flare until >=2 benched Metal targets reach 3 energy, then transition permanently to Archaludon
doctrines.discriminating_metric: A/B on first_attack_turn vs loss_share[prize]: milking lowers first_attack_turn variance & builds a 2nd loaded Archaludon but delays first Metal Defender and exposes Cinderace (1 prize, no lab protection)

doctrines.name: fast-transition
doctrines.plan: promote Archaludon the moment ONE bench Archaludon hits 3 metal; minimize Cinderace's board exposure
doctrines.discriminating_metric: A/B on first_attack_turn (earlier) vs post_ko_attack_rate (worse redundancy); compare energy_attach_share[190] concentration

tensions.balance: fire Turbo Flare while bench_Archaludon_metal < 3; on the first turn a bench Archaludon reaches metal>=3, retreat Cinderace and promote Archaludon permanently
allow non-essential digging (Explorer's Guidance / Ultra Ball / Pokegear) only while deckCount > D, D in {10,12,15,18}
once online, keep nonattacking_turn_rate below cap (Metal Defender at least once per 2 turns); do not over-stall a self-milling deck into deckout

hypotheses.claim: L0 uses Explorer's Guidance (mills 4/use), Ultra Ball (discards 2), Pokegear and Poke Pad unconditionally every turn; in this 300HP-wall deck games run long and it decks itself out.
hypotheses.direction: loss_share[deckout] must be low; deckCount at game end must stay > 0 in wins
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: gating digs too early starves the assembly of the Duraludon->Archaludon line and metal, raising brick rate / first_attack_turn
hypotheses.scenario: Mirror or slow control matchup. Archaludon walls behind Full Metal Lab + Jumbo Ice Cream; L0 fires Explorer's Guidance + Ultra Ball + Pokegear each turn; by ~turn 16 deckCount hits 0 and L0 loses on the empty-deck rule before taking the 6th prize.
hypotheses.pattern: yamagire: promote deck-return conditions + stop digging when deck is thin

hypotheses.claim: When Cinderace is in the opening hand alongside a real Basic (Duraludon/Relicanth), L0's setup-active pick chooses the real Basic; because Cinderace is a Stage2 with no Raboot in the deck it can NEVER be played from hand later (probe-verified), so the deck's only energy accelerator is lost for the entire game.
hypotheses.direction: conditional on Cinderace in opening hand, it should be placed in the Active Spot at setup ~100% of the time; energy_attach_share[666] > 0 early
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: forcing Cinderace active even when it will be immediately KO'd (Fire, no Full Metal Lab protection, 1 free prize) can occasionally be worse than a Duraludon open; keep it conditional on a benchable Duraludon line existing
hypotheses.scenario: Opening hand = Cinderace + Duraludon + energy. L0 opens Duraludon active and benches, holding Cinderace. Cinderace is now a permanent dead card; no Turbo Flare ever fires; Metal Defender online slips to turn 4-5 and the deck plays with no acceleration all game.
hypotheses.pattern: setup-active must preserve one-shot post-setup-unplayable enablers

hypotheses.claim: With Cinderace active and able to Turbo Flare (50 + accel), L0 keeps attacking with the current active and never retreats (retreat0=free) to promote a loaded Archaludon, so the deck outputs 50/turn instead of 220/turn. Observed: a greedy build never transitioned without explicit retreat code.
hypotheses.direction: once a bench Archaludon has metal>=3, the active should become Archaludon within 1 turn; Metal Defender use-rate should dominate Turbo Flare after mid phase

threshold.value: share of post-setup attacks that are Metal Defender >= 0.6 by turn 5

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: promoting too eagerly before enough bench targets are loaded reduces the number of pre-loaded Archaludon (worse chain/redundancy)
hypotheses.pattern: attack-priority equilibrium: promote the real finisher; scale-attack accel must yield once its job is done

hypotheses.claim: L0 attaches the manual energy to the displayed-max attacker (Archaludon 220 on bench) instead of the active Cinderace's single energy needed to fire Turbo Flare (which then floods 3 energy from deck), starving acceleration in the opening turns.
hypotheses.direction: on a turn where Cinderace is active with 0 energy and a Turbo Flare would fire, the manual attach should go to Cinderace

threshold.value: energy_attach_share[666] >= 1 attach within first 2 own-turns when Cinderace opens

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: over-feeding Cinderace beyond the 1 energy it needs wastes attaches that Archaludon needs to reach 3 metal
hypotheses.pattern: deck-specific feeding plan: first attach enables the accelerator, rest go to the finisher

hypotheses.claim: Boss's Orders gust is gated on active displayed damage >= 60; when Cinderace is active (displayed 50) L0 will not gust even when the real plan (promote Archaludon for a 220 KO) makes a gust lethal; conversely it may spend Boss's Orders with no valuable target.
hypotheses.direction: Boss's Orders should fire only when a benched target is KO-able by the intended Metal Defender and is worth pulling (prize value / role)
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: too strict a target filter leaves the 2 copies unused when a tempo gust would have won the prize race
hypotheses.pattern: gust by prize-value and REAL damage, not displayed damage of current active

hypotheses.claim: On KO of the active Archaludon, L0 promotes by highest displayed damage and can promote type-dead Relicanth (Razor Fin needs Fighting, deck has none -> can never attack) or an unloaded Duraludon, stranding the board.
hypotheses.direction: post-KO promotion must choose a loaded Metal attacker (Archaludon with metal>=3, else a Duraludon that can Hammer In); never Relicanth
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: requiring metal>=3 to promote can leave you with no legal promote and force Relicanth anyway; fall back to any Metal Pokemon before Relicanth
hypotheses.pattern: type-aware loaded-attacker promotion (distinguish wall/type-death from loaded by TYPE not count)

hypotheses.claim: Lillie's Determination fires only at hand <= 5 (L0 draw-supporter gate); this deck accumulates dead Cinderace copies and situational trainers, so a fat (>5) hand of junk never gets recycled, and conversely a fat hand of live cards gets needlessly shuffled away.
hypotheses.direction: Lillie should fire when the hand holds >=2 dead/useless cards (esp. surplus Cinderace) OR hand is starved, not on a raw size threshold

threshold.value: play_rate[1227] in [0.3, 0.6]; dead-card-in-hand turns should trend down after firing

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: firing Lillie too often reshuffles metal/pieces you wanted to hold and thins the deck faster (feeds H1)
hypotheses.pattern: fire condition on held-state (dead-card count) not generic hand-size threshold

hypotheses.claim: Jumbo Ice Cream (heal 80, requires active with 3+ energy = Archaludon) is undervalued by L0, so Archaludon dies a turn earlier than needed, degrading the 2-prize wall trade.
hypotheses.direction: Jumbo Ice Cream should fire when healing 80 keeps Archaludon above the opponent's next-hit lethal threshold

threshold.value: play_rate[1147] >= 0.4 in games reaching mid phase

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: healing when it does not change survival wastes the item and a turn action
hypotheses.pattern: heal gated on survival-threshold state, not generic

hypotheses.claim: The single ACE SPEC Hero's Cape (+100HP) is misattached by L0 to the current active (e.g., Cinderace) instead of Archaludon, wasting the one-per-deck resource that turns Archaludon into a 400HP wall.
hypotheses.direction: Hero's Cape should attach only to an Archaludon that is or will be the active wall
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: holding Cape for a perfect target can leave it stranded in hand if Archaludon keeps getting replaced
hypotheses.pattern: tool target restricted to the win-condition pokemon

hypotheses.claim: Full Metal Lab is a defensive stadium that L0 may fail to keep on the field (not re-playing after the opponent replaces it) or may not prioritize, losing the -30 damage reduction that keeps the Metal wall alive.
hypotheses.direction: self Full Metal Lab should be in play whenever a Metal Pokemon is active and no self-stadium is down and a copy is available
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: spamming the stadium every turn burns the 4 copies and a card action when the current one already suffices
hypotheses.pattern: maintain defensive stadium uptime by held-state, not blind replay
